summary: No rules problem, and the port is mechanically sound: it is the same kernel and tile check as prefill master, with both configs compiled before capture. But the mechanism is quantitatively weak. On this routing generator Marlin runs only about 15-18% more m-blocks than the swap-AB kernel runs tiles, and prefill already measured this kernel's per-tile cost at about 2x Marlin's per-m-block cost here. Expect stage 1 to be about 1.5-2x slower on the replaced kernels, not faster. Run it as a rewrite stage, with BLOCK_T=64 at bs=256 too, and treat milestone 2 as unlikely until the dequant gets cheaper.
justification: Shapes. I re-simulated reference.generate_input (numpy, normal dist, rank=busiest, 200 seeds). bs=128 gives 22.8 distinct local experts and about 192 local routes (max expert about 56 rows, the rest mostly 3-15 rows). bs=256 gives 24.7 distinct experts and about 388 routes (max about 116). This agrees with the TASK floors: 101.3/108.9 us means 0.75 x distinct x 27.4 MB, so about 23.6/25.3 distinct. Tile counts: Marlin block 16 at bs=128 runs 27.2 m-blocks vs 23.1 swap-AB tiles at BLOCK_T=64. Marlin block 32 at bs=256 runs 29.4 m-blocks vs 25.1 tiles at BLOCK_T=128. So the redundancy this hypothesis removes is about 15-18% of tile count, not the multi-x the 'few hot experts carry most routes' story implies. Student-t popularity at scale 0.03 is mild, and most touched experts get a single small block either way. Per-unit cost: master's profile gives Marlin about 316/27.2 = 11.6 us per 16-row m-block at bs=128 and 490/29.4 = 16.7 us per 32-row m-block at bs=256. Prefill measured this exact kernel and config (BLOCK_T=64, 4 warps, 3 stages, same H=I=4096 NVFP4 weights) at about 25 us per expert-tile at turn_1, with a full grid (32 experts x 64 W-tiles, similar to the ~1500 CTAs here). The BLOCK_T=128 / 8-warp config cost more per tile at turn_4 (about 2.1 ms total). Projection: bs=128 is about 23 x 25 = 575 us vs 316 (about 1.8x slower). bs=256 at BLOCK_T=128 is about 25 tiles at more than 25 us each, so 650-1000 us vs 490. Each tile's dequant work is fixed by BLOCK_W x K and does not shrink with real rows: masked activation rows save HBM bytes, not dequant ALU or MMA. Parity at bs=128 needs per-tile cost of 13.7 us or less, a 1.8x improvement. Milestone 3 (1.5x floor, about 150 us) needs about 6.5 us per tile, close to the 5.7 us HBM time for one expert. That is reachable in principle only with Marlin-class packed dequant (lop3/prmt, 8 codes per int32), which the Risk section lists as a stage-2 option. Weakest link: the claim that Marlin's per-m-block re-dequant/re-stream is the dominant waste. The routing data shows few extra m-blocks, and the per-tile dequant cost (where Triton is about 2x behind Marlin) dominates instead. Second weak point: the bs>128 config is 'prefill's measured one' only nominally. BLOCK_T=128 was tuned for about 94 rows per expert, while here a typical expert has about 15 rows, so most of each 128-column MMA is padding. BLOCK_T=64 at bs=256 gives 26.2 tiles vs 25.1 (+4%) with half the MMA and the cheaper 4-warp config, so it is the better stage-1 pick. The expected 'faster' directions for bs=128 and bs=256 should read 'slower (stage 1), per-tile cost is the readout'. The flat controls at bs<128 are correct: those shapes are byte-identical to master.
confounders: marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm: the incumbent this is judged against is the tuned Marlin (block 16/32 at bs=128/256, about 9-11% faster than SGLang's 48/64 pick). That raises the bar but does not confound attribution, because the milestone compares the _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel rows against master's 316.1/490.2 us Marlin rows directly. Note that against SGLang's untuned 48/64 Marlin the redundancy story would look stronger (bs=128 at block 48 is about 23-24 m-blocks of a more expensive class), so do not reuse SGLang's verify numbers as the incumbent.

sglang-marlin-path-parity: it supplies moe_align_block_size(local_ids, bsm, 32). With count 32 instead of prefill's 256, the static capacity, and so the grid of early-exit CTAs, is about 8x smaller at BLOCK_T=64/128. That helps Triton slightly vs prefill's setup, so the prefill per-tile cost is if anything a slight overestimate. No attribution problem.
post-expert-norm-triton-small-m and triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack: both gate on num_tokens <= 32 or < 32, so they are not on the bs>=128 path. No interaction.
interference: No companions. This is kind: rewrite, judged on the replaced kernels' own profile rows at bs=128/256. Those rows are directly readable (two _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel rows vs master's Marlin rows), and the bs<128 shapes are byte-identical controls. No landed hypothesis shares the bs>=128 GEMM path except the block-m pick, which this change removes. An ab-revert of that pick would only change the incumbent, not this kernel's time. Per-tile cost is the stage readout, and the next stage (packed dequant) is the follow-up. A BLOCK_T control is better folded into stage 1 as a spec edit (BLOCK_T=64 at all num_tokens >= 128) than spent as a separate check while moe has 4 checks left.
rules_flags: None blocking. The nibble reorder is a lossless permutation of the E2M1 codes (asserted per expert in _reorder_nibbles), the scales stay e4m3/fp32 as stored, and the dequant happens in registers, per the user's no-BF16-copy ruling. The bank is built from weights only in prepare(). Nothing derived from data is cached, and the branch is on num_tokens only.

Make sure _check_expert_gemms runs every (config x w13/w2 x ZERO_NONLOCAL) variant kernel_fn can launch (N=8192/TOP_K=8/False and N=4096/TOP_K=1/True for each BLOCK_T used), so nothing JIT-compiles during graph capture. If BLOCK_T=64 is used at bs=256, only one config needs compiling. Prefill's version uses LOCAL_EXPERTS-1 and orig = weights[name] directly. Here the weights hold 256 experts, so slice to [0, 32) consistently for both the bank and the check's reference (expert index e must address the same expert in both).
The prepare-time prints (n_regs/n_spills) and torch.cuda.synchronize stay in prepare(). Nothing is printed or synced inside kernel_fn.
cache3 aliases cache1 (cache13) as on master. The Triton w2 call reads only cache2, so this is safe, but keep the w13 -> silu -> w2 order and do not let w2 read cache1.
open_questions: Should stage 1 use BLOCK_T=64 at bs=256/257 too? The simulation gives 26.2 tiles vs 25.1 at BLOCK_T=128, with half the padding MMA and the cheaper 4-warp config. I recommend editing the spec before claim. bs=257 then has a capacity of 2056+32*63 slots, which is fine.

Is a check worth spending when the per-tile cost is already known from prefill (same kernel, config and weights)? The new information is only the low-rows-per-expert regime, where the per-tile cost should be the same because the dequant is per weight tile. If checks are scarce, consider minting stage 1 with the packed lop3/prmt-style dequant already included. That is the only lever that addresses the dominant cost.

Does SGLang's moe_align_block_size(..., 32) give the -1 routes blocks of their own (block_experts == -1)? If not, ZERO_NONLOCAL_W2 never fires and the remote cache3 rows stay stale. That is fine only because fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum skips slot_expert_ids == -1, as it does on master.
